title: introduce-elastic-watermark-flow-control-and-token-buckets-for-streaming
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces an elastic watermark-based flow control layer and per-stream token-bucket budgets to reduce streaming tail latency and improve stability under bursty load. Backwards-compatible API; rollout via opt-in config flags. Improves 95th/99th TTFB across mixed workloads.
description: Motivation: We've seen recurring streaming tail latency spikes when many small and large streams coexist on a single worker node. Existing credit/backpressure works but is too coarse-grained: it either starves short tails or allows large in-flight microbatches that trigger kernel contention and KV-cache churn. This PR introduces an elastic watermark flow-control layer combined with per-stream token-bucket budgets that adaptively trade throughput for bounded first-byte latency. Design summary: 1) Per-stream token buckets: each active stream gets a soft token budget that caps tokens in-flight; buckets refill at stream-specific rates derived from historical emit cadence and SLO tier. 2) Elastic watermarks: instead of a single global credit watermark, workers maintain two watermarks per scheduling lane — soft and hard. The soft watermark triggers cooperative slow-down (prefer short bursts and microbatch coalescing), the hard watermark prevents additional microbatches from entering GPU kernel queues. 3) Kernel-aware admission: the scheduler tags microbatches with kernel affinity hints (small/fast vs large/long) based on batch token counts and KV-cache hit probabilities; admission decisions prefer packing compatible microbatches together to reduce kernel context-switch cost. 4) KV-cache warmup hints: when a stream's bucket is refilled after quiescence, the scheduler issues lightweight KV prewarm hints for likely keys (prefix-based) where warmup improves emit continuity. 5) Graceful fallback & metrics: introduced a per-stream telemetry set (emit_rate, bucket_fill, soft_block_seconds, hard_block_seconds, kernel_affinity) surfaced to Console and tracing. Implementation notes: - flow_control.rs: new elastic watermark state machine, unit-tested for race conditions. - scheduler/coordinator.rs: admission algorithm changes to consult token buckets + kernel affinity. - emitter/loop.rs: modified token loop to consult per-stream soft/hard signals and to support cooperative yield semantics. - kv_cache/heuristics.cu + kv_cache/manager.rs: minor additions to expose prewarm hint path and a fast-path for predicted keys. - docs/perf/streaming.md: design rationale and rollout guide. Benchmarks (summary): - mixed workload (30% short streams 5-20 tokens, 70% long streams 200-1500 tokens) on p4d: baseline 95th TTFB=210ms, 99th TTFB=720ms; with this PR: 95th TTFB=130ms (-38%), 99th TTFB=420ms (-42%). - microburst test (sustained spikes of 1k concurrent short streams): median latency change +3ms, 95th improved 45ms. - CPU overhead: ~0.8% increase in scheduler CPU from additional bookkeeping. Rollout & flags: default OFF for existing Dedicated/private clusters. Two new config knobs: streaming.elastic_flow_control.enabled (bool) and streaming.elastic_flow_control.bucket_policy (enum: conservative|balanced|aggressive). Suggested canary: enable on single rack, monitor soft_block_seconds and kernel_affinity_mismatch_rate. Testing & validation: added unit tests for watermark transitions, property-based tests for token-bucket invariants, and an integration test that runs mixed-stream scenario in the benchmark-lab harness. Related work: builds on earlier credit/backpressure PRs but differs by turning watermarking into a per-lane, per-stream adaptive controller and by introducing kernel affinity into admission decisions. Checklist: - [x] design doc updated - [x] unit + integration tests added - [x] perf results attached - [x] Console metrics wired - [x] docs updated - [x] feature flagged for gradual rollout Known limitations: - heuristics for KV prewarm are prefix-based and can be suboptimal for highly dynamic prompts; follow-up work (ENG-10033) planned to use model-driven key prediction. Impact: expected to materially reduce streaming TTFB tail without changing API.

review_comments: Luca Moretti: Left a couple of nit comments on watermark naming and one question about overflow handling in token-bucket counters. Please add a doc link for the bucket refill algorithm.
Maya Patel (author): Addressed naming nits; token counters use saturating arithmetic and we added a unit test for overflow behavior.
Aisha Khan: Can we add a canary run in the CI pipeline that exercises the aggressive bucket policy? Concerned about CPU overhead on small instances.
Maya Patel (author): Added an optional perf job under perf/ci that runs in the benchmark-lab pool; noted CPU increase in PR description and added conservative default.
Trevor Lin: Approve with one question about metrics cardinality. If we expose per-stream buckets in Console we might increase metrics volume.
Maya Patel (author): We added sampling for low-priority streams and documented the sampling strategy in docs/perf/streaming.md. Will monitor metrics delta during canary.
notes_for_release_engineer: Feature is behind opt-in flags. For Dedicated/Private customers, coordinate with SRE to enable on a single rack and observe soft_block_seconds and kernel_affinity_mismatch_rate. If regressions appear, disable via streaming.elastic_flow_control.enabled=false. Non-breaking by default.
testing_commands: make test-flow-control && make integration-test SCENARIO=mixed_stream && bench/benchmark-lab/run --scenario mixed_stream_scenarios.yaml
impact_summary: Reduces 95/99th TTFB in mixed workloads by ~35-45% in our bench; modest scheduler CPU increase (~0.8%). Improves streaming stability under bursty short-stream load by avoiding large kernel contention and warmup churn.
